had a loose target for a small thing. finished it early.
started something new before finishing the last thing.
read the manual for something I've used for years.
I'd have said open-ended time was the ideal condition. what actually happens is I second-guess every choice for weeks and arrive back where I started.
the first version, usually. after a month of it.
tried to explain it to someone and heard how odd it sounds.
gave up after ten minutes and made tea instead.
sharpened everything that could be sharpened.
had open time for something purely technical. went fine.
found an old recording I'd forgotten making.
swapped one component for a nearly identical one.
spent the session on a bit nobody will ever notice.
wrote a list of things to learn. filed the list.
did it badly on purpose to see what happened.
the two things of mine I'd stand over were both done against something immovable, where there was no time to reconsider anything.
both. and I fought the deadline at the time.
cleared the workspace properly for the first time in months.
tried the thing everyone recommends. hated it.
counted how many of these I actually own.
did a slow warm-up and nothing else.
